question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer, proposed CIO of 'Saraswati Opportunities Fund', is finalising the Trust Deed and LLP-Manager structure. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012, which of the following is an accurate statement on the compulsory registration requirement for all AIFs domiciled in India?

answer.text: Only close-ended AIFs with corpus exceeding INR 100 crore are required to register; smaller funds may operate as unregistered pools.
AIFs domiciled in IFSC/GIFT City are exempt from SEBI registration and are regulated solely by IFSCA with no SEBI oversight.
An AIF can commence investment activities immediately on filing Form A; registration with SEBI can be completed within 24 months from first close.

All existing and proposed AIFs domiciled in India are subject to compulsory registration with SEBI; existing schemes may complete their agreed tenure but cannot raise fresh monies beyond commitments already made until registration is granted.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Regulation 3 of SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012, every AIF domiciled in India must compulsorily register with SEBI. Existing schemes are grandfathered to complete tenure but cannot raise fresh monies beyond existing commitments until registration. Penalty under Section 15EA of SEBI Act for non-compliance is minimum INR 1 lakh, up to INR 1 crore or 3x gains. **The Trap:** Option B fabricates a corpus threshold that does not exist. Option C is wrong — IFSC AIFs have some relaxations but are still within SEBI's and IFSCA's joint regulatory perimeter. Option D inverts the sequence — money cannot be called before receipt of Registration Certificate; only commitments can be accepted post in-principle approval. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/XIX-B (Distributor exams) test this from a selling-is-permitted-only-for-registered-AIFs angle. XIX-C tests it from a Manager compliance-filing and applicability angle. Also appears in III-A/C Compliance exams. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Manager tip: Between Form A filing and grant of Registration Certificate, the fund can sign contribution agreements and accept commitments (post in-principle approval) but must not draw down capital. Sequencing the SCORES/SEBI Login, custody account, and bank account opening in this window is critical so that first drawdown can occur on Day 1 of Registration.
